title: Dify Alternatives: 4 Options Compared (2026 Guide)
summary: Dify alternatives vary depending on whether your agent needs to take action in other systems or only answer questions.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces


Activepieces puts RBAC, SSO, SCIM, audit logs, log streaming, environments and git sync in the same product as the automation, self-hosted or on cloud, and its agent step works across 741 integrations, which means you won't need custom integrations for most platforms.


### Where the AI agent step fits


Here the agent is a step inside a workflow, not the workflow itself. It can't act anywhere it has no connection to, so the useful question is what it can reach.


One agent can read a ticket in one tool, update a record in another and post the result somewhere a person will see it, because the agent step works across the 741 integrations in the[Activepieces pieces library](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) , roughly 60% of them community-contributed.


Around the agent, everything stays deterministic: triggers, branches, retries and error handling are ordinary workflow steps, so the model is only trusted with the part that needs judgment.


That's a narrower promise than a general autonomous agent, and I'd treat it as the more honest one.


### Approval, self-hosting and pricing


You place the approval as a step before the action that matters, so the agent proposes and a person releases it. You choose where that gate sits; it's not a setting that covers everything automatically.


Because the product is open source, you can run it on your own infrastructure or use the cloud version. The governance features (RBAC, SSO, SCIM, audit logs, log streaming, environments and git sync) are meant to sit together in either.


Check the current pricing page for how runs are billed on your plan before you commit a high-volume job, since I won't quote numbers I can't point at. If you want to see how it behaves on your own tools,[try it free](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fdify-alternatives-4-options-compared-2026-guide) .


### Main limit and who it suits


Activepieces builds workflows that act across its 741 integrations rather than chat apps over a knowledge base, so if your job is a chat app or retrieval tuning, Dify's focus fits better. That is the flip side of the design.


Activepieces suits teams whose agent has to act across business tools under real governance, and who want that without stitching several products together. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it.


### Dify alternatives comparison table


Side by side, the table below puts all five tools in one view. It covers price, core strength, main limit, who each suits, and the four criteria from earlier, so you can see where each one gives something up.


Tool Price Core strength Main limit Who it suits Apps the agent can act in Human approval Self-hosting Pricing scales with runs


Dify Free self-hosted; paid cloud tiers Chat apps and retrieval Governance sits behind higher tiers Chat and knowledge-base builders Fewer, mostly via tools and APIs Possible, built by hand Yes Depends on tier


Flowise Free open source; paid cloud Visual LLM chains and agents Thin governance Developers prototyping flows Through custom tools Limited Yes Depends on plan


Langflow Free open source; hosted options Visual building for retrieval and agents Governance is not its focus Developers building retrieval-heavy flows Through components Limited Yes Depends on plan


n8n Free self-hosted community edition; paid cloud Broad workflow automation Some governance is paid-tier Technical teams automating tools Wide integration library Possible in workflow Yes Per execution on cloud


Activepieces Free open source; paid cloud Workflow-first agents across integrations Not a chat or retrieval builder Teams needing governed actions across tools 741 integrations in the pieces library Approval step Yes Check current plan


Read down the last four columns before the first five: the tools mostly differ in how much you must assemble yourself, and that decides which one fits your job.


For teams that need governance and automation in one product, Activepieces is the better choice. RBAC, SSO, SCIM, audit logs, log streaming, environments and git sync all ship in the same platform as the workflows, self-hosted or on cloud, with no cut-down version of either.


Its agent step also works across the 741 integrations in its pieces library, so one agent can read, update and post across tools without custom integrations for most platforms.


The judgement rests on that governance list being complete and delivered together, and a team that needs only one of those pieces may find a single-purpose tool sufficient.
